statement: Let n = len(nums). Define a subarray [l,u), with 0 <= l < u <= n, to be special when the bitwise OR of nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[u-1], interpreted as a non-negative integer, is at least k. The function returns a result r and: if at least one special subarray exists, then r is the minimum of u-l over all special subarrays [l,u); equivalently, r >= 1, some special subarray has length r, and no special subarray has length less than r. If no special subarray exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: The function returns a result r and does not fail: for every input satisfying the preconditions there is no panic, no out-of-bounds access, and no signed 64-bit overflow.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r != -1 if and only if there exist integers l and u with 0 <= l < u <= len(nums) such that the bitwise OR of nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[u-1] is at least k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let n = len(nums) and let O be the bitwise OR of all elements nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[n-1]. Then r = -1 if and only if O < k; equivalently, r != -1 if and only if O >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 1, there exists an integer l such that 0 <= l, l+r <= len(nums), and the bitwise OR of nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[l+r-1] is at least k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 1, for every pair of integers l,u with 0 <= l < u <= len(nums), if the bitwise OR of nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[u-1] is at least k, then u-l >= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if and only if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r > 1, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] < k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r = -1, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] < k.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and k = 0, r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if k > 0 and nums[i] = 0 for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then r = -1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and len(nums) = 1, r = 1 if nums[0] >= k, and r = -1 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000,000; and 0 <= k <= 1,000,000,000.
